$comment: VERSIONED CONTENT, NOT CODE (Carl, 5-7 Sep 2026; hard rule 14). WHICH PEOPLE AT A LOCATION MAY BE THE PROVIDER ON AN AGREEMENT. The provider named on an assignment of benefit is the SERVICING PROVIDER whose provider number goes on the claim -- never, of itself, the person who delivered the service. A practice nurse working on 'for and on behalf of' items delivers the service and bills nothing under their own number; the claim, and therefore the assignment, goes under the GP. A phlebotomist generates no Medicare claim from the practice at all. So the role is a property of the PRACTITIONER AT A LOCATION (an Affiliation), because a provider number is issued per practitioner per location and a nurse practitioner at one site may be an RN at another. Order here IS the order on screen. THE DISPLAY WORDS ARE NOT HERE: they live in the string table keyed by `key` (REQ-LANG-01/-02). Bump `version` on every edit. WHAT THIS FILE CANNOT DO: it cannot let a non-GP hold an enduring agreement. Enduring is GP-only (hard rule 6, REQ-END-01a) and that is checked in code against the provider TYPE as well as the role -- a nurse practitioner is a servicing provider and is still not a GP. Adding a role with `mayBeProviderOnAgreement: true` widens who may be named on an EPISODIC agreement and nothing else.
$secondFlagComment: THE SECOND FLAG ANSWERS A SECOND QUESTION (Carl, 12 Sep 2026; ARRIVAL-WHO-IS-SEEN.md section 3). `mayBeProviderOnAgreement` says whether THIS person may be named on the contract. `servicesNeedABillingProvider` says whether a service delivered by somebody in this role needs a billing provider named AT ALL before an agreement can exist. The two are not the same question and the three roles give three different pairs: a servicing provider needs one and IS one; a nurse working under a provider needs one and is not one, so the arrival is recorded and waits for the supervising provider to be named; a phlebotomist taking bloods generates no Medicare claim from the practice, so no billing provider is needed, no agreement is drafted, and the visit decision `none` is a correct and complete answer rather than a gap. Before this flag existed the second and third cases were indistinguishable and both were REFUSED, which meant a patient who came only for a specimen collection could not be arrived at all. THE FLAG IS NOT A BILLING JUDGEMENT AND THE PLATFORM MAKES NONE: it does not say who may claim for a specimen collection, only whether this platform must wait for a provider number before it can produce a contract. A role that may be the provider on an agreement must also need one -- itself -- and the loader refuses a file that says otherwise.
